terms.plainEnglish: Installs packages listed in package.json so the project can run.
terms.beginnerExplanation: npm install downloads the packages this project needs.
terms.learningExplanation: npm install reads package.json and package-lock.json, then installs dependencies into node_modules.
terms.advancedExplanation: npm install resolves and materializes the dependency graph while updating the lockfile when needed.
terms.confusion: It may update lockfiles. That is normal for package installs.

terms.plainEnglish: Runs the project's development script from package.json.
terms.beginnerExplanation: npm run dev usually starts the app while you are building it.
terms.learningExplanation: npm run dev runs the dev script defined in package.json.
terms.advancedExplanation: npm run dev invokes the configured package script in npm's script environment.
terms.confusion: The script must exist in package.json or npm will report a missing script.

terms.plainEnglish: Runs the project's build script, usually to create production-ready output.
terms.beginnerExplanation: npm run build creates the version of the app meant for release or deployment.
terms.learningExplanation: npm run build runs the build script from package.json, often creating optimized output.
terms.advancedExplanation: npm run build invokes the project's production build pipeline.
terms.confusion: Building does not usually start the app for local editing.

terms.plainEnglish: The main file that lists project scripts, dependencies, and package metadata.
terms.beginnerExplanation: package.json is the project file that lists commands and installed packages.
terms.learningExplanation: package.json stores metadata, scripts, dependencies, and development tools for a Node project.
terms.advancedExplanation: package.json is npm's project manifest for scripts, package metadata, and dependency declarations.
terms.confusion: Editing package.json manually can be useful, but invalid JSON will break npm commands.

terms.plainEnglish: Packages the app usually needs when it runs.
terms.beginnerExplanation: dependencies are packages the app needs to work.
terms.learningExplanation: dependencies are runtime packages required by the application or library.
terms.advancedExplanation: dependencies are installed as production dependency declarations for consumers or runtime execution.
terms.confusion: Dependencies are different from devDependencies, which are mostly tools used while building.

terms.plainEnglish: Packages mostly used during development, checking, or building.
terms.beginnerExplanation: devDependencies are tools you mostly use while building the project.
terms.learningExplanation: devDependencies are packages for development, tests, type checking, linting, or builds.
terms.advancedExplanation: devDependencies declare tooling dependencies that are generally not needed by production runtime consumers.
terms.confusion: A package can work from either section, but the distinction helps describe why it is installed.

commands.whatItDoes: Installs the packages listed in package.json so the project can run.

parts.explanation: Downloads and installs the project's dependencies.

commands.whenToUse: Use this after cloning a Node project or when package.json changes.
commands.commonMistake: Do not edit node_modules by hand. Change package.json and run npm install instead.

commands.whatItDoes: Runs the project's compile script from package.json.

parts.explanation: Runs a named script from package.json.
The script name. In this project, it compiles TypeScript.

commands.whenToUse: Use this when you want to check that TypeScript builds successfully.
commands.commonMistake: The script must exist in package.json. If it does not, npm will report a missing script.

commands.whatItDoes: Runs the project's development script from package.json, usually starting a local dev server or watcher.

parts.explanation: Runs a named script from package.json.
The script name, commonly used for development mode.

commands.whenToUse: Use this while building an app when the project provides a dev script.
commands.commonMistake: Not every project has npm run dev. Check package.json if the command fails.
